Metadata.Purpose: Executive summary consultant input for current Versetal assessments and a reusable baseline for future AD migration assessments.
Metadata.ReuseGuidance: Copy this file for future customers, update Metadata.CustomerName, review Defaults, and replace or add PerForest entries for each assessed source or target forest.

Defaults.ScopeNote: Migration scope should be confirmed with business, application, and identity stakeholders before final wave planning is approved.
Defaults.DnsOverlapAssessment: No automated DNS zone overlap analysis was performed in this discovery set. Validate namespace ownership, conditional forwarders, suffix routing, and application name-resolution dependencies during migration planning.
Defaults.HybridIdentityConsiderations: Hybrid identity was not directly assessed in this AD-only discovery run. Confirm Entra Connect or Cloud Sync topology, federation assumptions, tenant alignment, and source-of-authority ownership separately.

RecommendedMigrationApproach.DirectoryMigrationTool: ADMT inter-forest migration tooling. If there is a need to maintain profile son Desktops we will need a tool like Profile Wizard from ForensIT
RecommendedMigrationApproach.Notes: Use pilot waves for privileged accounts, service accounts, and representative user and device cohorts before broader migration waves.

AdditionalComplexityDrivers: Application authentication and service dependency mapping should be completed before cutover sequencing is finalized.
Namespace normalization and target landing-zone standards should be reviewed before broad migration waves begin.
AdditionalRisks: Consultant review is still required for DNS forwarding, namespace overlap, and application authentication dependencies.
Business-unit migration waves and rollback expectations should be confirmed before execution planning is finalized.

rossoptical.local.ScopeNote: This source forest is a focused single-domain migration scope into the target landing zone and is well suited to a controlled staged migration once identity cleanup activities are complete.

RecommendedMigrationApproach.Notes: Resolve duplicate identities, validate service-account dependencies, and normalize user namespaces before broader user, workstation, and server waves.

AdditionalComplexityDrivers: Namespace normalization is a leading complexity driver because most inventoried accounts use non-routable UPN suffixes.
Identity-conflict resolution with the target environment should be completed before production migration waves are scheduled.
Privileged and protected accounts should be separated into dedicated migration and validation waves.
AdditionalRisks: Source identities overlap with the target environment and should be remediated before migration execution.
Non-routable UPN usage should be corrected before final identity synchronization or cutover planning.
Service-account dependencies require application-owner validation before server or application migration waves begin.

ReadinessOverride.Note: Proceed after identity conflict resolution, service-account validation, and namespace normalization are reviewed and approved with customer stakeholders.

lighthouseoptics.local.ScopeNote: This source forest has a larger user and device footprint than rossoptical and should be planned as a staged migration sequence into the target environment.

RecommendedMigrationApproach.Notes: Use pilot waves to validate privileged access handling, service-account dependencies, and representative device migration patterns before broader production waves.

AdditionalComplexityDrivers: Higher object volume increases coordination, validation, and rollback-planning requirements.
Policy, OU, and privileged-access review should be completed before migration targeting is locked.
Cross-source and source-to-target identity overlap should be validated in the shared comparison workspace before execution planning.
AdditionalRisks: Identity overlap with the target and across source environments should be reviewed before migration waves are approved.
Privileged and service-account dependencies may affect sequencing for application and infrastructure workloads.
Namespace and hybrid-identity assumptions still require consultant confirmation before cutover design is finalized.

poc.local.ScopeNote: This forest serves as the target landing zone and should be validated for namespace, access, and policy readiness before onboarding production source identities.

RecommendedMigrationApproach.DirectoryMigrationTool: Target landing zone for ADMT inter-forest migration waves
RecommendedMigrationApproach.Notes: Validate OU design, GPO targeting, privileged access model, and target naming standards before onboarding production users, groups, and devices.

AdditionalComplexityDrivers: Target standards for OU placement, policy application, and delegated administration should be finalized before execution.
Target namespace, DNS forwarding, and landing-zone assumptions should be validated before source cutover planning.
AdditionalRisks: Target design assumptions should be reviewed against source application and authentication dependencies before production onboarding.
Hybrid identity, source-of-authority, and target tenant expectations should be confirmed before production wave scheduling.
